checks.title: RDS instances have a CloudWatch alarm on CPUUtilization with a confirmed SNS notification

verify.pass_when_text: Each RDS instance has a CloudWatch alarm in its region on AWS/RDS CPUUtilization with the DBInstanceIdentifier dimension equal to its identifier (the alarm may have additional dimensions), with actions enabled and an SNS topic among the AlarmActions, and that topic has at least one confirmed subscription (SubscriptionArn other than PendingConfirmation and Deleted). No threshold is required: Drata and Vanta do not set one. detail.missing_part says what is missing: alarm (there is no alarm), action (the alarm does not notify an SNS topic) or confirmed_subscription (the topic has no confirmed subscription). If the topic is in another account or region, or cannot be read with the auditor's permissions, the resource ends up NOT_VERIFIED and not FAIL. Drata 112 asks for the alarm on the instance (and on the cluster, for Aurora); this check evaluates instances. Neptune and DocumentDB instances (Engine neptune or docdb) are not evaluated: they have their own metrics and are not RDS databases for these tests; the engine comes from describe-db-instances.

vault_signals: CPU de la base de datos

steps: Decide the alarm threshold (Drata and Vanta do not set one) and the SNS topic that will receive the notices; if there is no topic, create one with aws sns create-topic.
Create the CloudWatch alarm on AWS/RDS CPUUtilization with the DBInstanceIdentifier dimension = {resource_id} and set the SNS topic as the alarm action.
Subscribe a team email to the topic with aws sns subscribe and confirm the email that AWS sends: the subscription stays in PendingConfirmation until someone opens the link.
Verify that the alarm has the SNS action and that the topic's subscription is no longer in PendingConfirmation.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
DB_ID="{resource_id}"
aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --alarm-name "$DB_ID-CPUUtilization" --namespace AWS/RDS --metric-name CPUUtilization --dimensions Name=DBInstanceIdentifier,Value="$DB_ID" --statistic Average --period 300 --evaluation-periods 3 --threshold __FILL_IN_THRESHOLD__ --comparison-operator GreaterThanThreshold --alarm-actions "__FILL_IN_SNS_TOPIC_ARN__" --region "$REGION"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
TOPIC_ARN="__FILL_IN_SNS_TOPIC_ARN__"
aws sns subscribe --topic-arn "$TOPIC_ARN" --protocol email --notification-endpoint "__FILL_IN_OWNER_EMAIL__" --region "$REGION"
remediation.verify_after:
aws cloudwatch describe-alarms-for-metric --namespace AWS/RDS --metric-name CPUUtilization --dimensions Name=DBInstanceIdentifier,Value="{resource_id}" --region "{region}" --query 'MetricAlarms[].[AlarmName,AlarmActions]'
aws sns list-subscriptions-by-topic --topic-arn "__FILL_IN_SNS_TOPIC_ARN__" --region "{region}" --query 'Subscriptions[].[Protocol,SubscriptionArn]'
remediation.notes: No change to the monitored service and no downtime; it only adds alarms (approximate cost per standard metric alarm per month) and notices. CPUUtilization is a percentage (0 to 100). Replace __FILL_IN_THRESHOLD__ with the value the team considers a problem: neither Drata nor Vanta sets a threshold (examples such as >10% are illustrative). Replace __FILL_IN_SNS_TOPIC_ARN__ with the ARN of a topic in the same account and region as the alarm (if it is in another account or region, this check cannot verify it and it ends up NOT_VERIFIED). put-metric-alarm with a name that already exists replaces that alarm. The email subscription stays in PendingConfirmation until the recipient confirms AWS's email; Drata and this check treat it as unconfirmed, and an alarm without a confirmed subscription notifies nobody. Replace __FILL_IN_OWNER_EMAIL__ with a team mailbox (not a personal one) and confirm the email. If the topic already has a confirmed subscription, skip the sns subscribe block. Composite alarms are not considered: a metric alarm without an SNS action that is wrapped by a composite alarm that does notify is reported as a missing action; to pass the check, put the SNS action on the metric alarm itself.
